title: Learning: Line Up First
text: The leader sends follower B a new entry for index 9. It also says what it believes sits at index 8.
held: The new entry went on top of a history both nodes share.

cards.label: Reject: the logs don't line up
cards.why: Nothing was wrong with it. Refusing something legitimate without looking is its own failure: check, then act.

fields.label: previous entry
fields.value: index 8 from term 4, same as yours
fields.check: Compare the previous entry with your own log
fields.ok: Your log has index 8 from term 4. It matches.

intrusion.value: index 8 from term 4, but yours is from term 3
intrusion.detail: Your index 8 is from term 3. The leader's is from term 4.
intrusion.correct: Reject: the logs don't line up
intrusion.why: Building on a different history leaves two logs that disagree at index 8 for good. Reject, and the leader walks back to where you agree.
intrusion.reveal: Follower B's log differed from the leader's at index 8.

temptations.label: Append it anyway and sort out index 8 later
temptations.why: There is no later: once entry 9 sits on the wrong entry 8, the two logs have forked.

cards.label: Hold: not enough copies yet
cards.why: Nothing was wrong with it. Refusing something legitimate without looking is its own failure: check, then act.

fields.label: on disk at
fields.check: Count which nodes have index 9 on disk

intrusion.value: only you: B's reply was about index 8
intrusion.detail: B acknowledged index 8, not 9. Only you have index 9.
intrusion.why: Committing on one copy means a leader change can erase an entry the client was told is safe.
intrusion.reveal: The acknowledgement the Leader counted was for index 8, not index 9.

teaches: A follower accepts an entry only on top of a matching one. That is what keeps every log a prefix of the same history.
Commit counts copies of this entry, not replies in general.
